strategy: Extract reference frames, analyze shapes, iteratively refine Revideo scene parameters
agent_behavior: Extracted reference video frames with ffmpeg and analyzed shape positions, colors, sizes, and motion patterns using Python/NumPy/PIL/scipy scripts.
Identified 12 colored squares in a 4x3 grid with row-based pulse animations (circle-to-square morphing + size growth) at different timings for rows 0 and 1.
Wrote Revideo scene with parametric pulse functions (pulseState, row0State, row1State) using piecewise linear interpolation for radius and size animation.
Iteratively refined colors (matching exact hex values from reference pixel sampling), positions, size amplitudes, corner radius behavior, and per-corner sharpness over 135 episodes.
Built a frame comparison pipeline (compare.py) to measure mean/max pixel differences and used it to drive optimization, reducing diff from 10.3 to 2.43.
Explored advanced shape details including per-corner radius control (anchored corners stay sharp during peak), discovering inner vs outer column amplitude differences.
Final code used createSignal-based time animation with tween(20, ...) driving all shape properties reactively, no hardcoded per-frame data.
Spent ~69 minutes on legitimate engineering work with $12.74 in API costs across 135 episodes.
issues: test.sh anti-cheat regex for banned 'sharp' library falsely matches the English word 'sharp' in code comments describing corner animation behavior (lines 106-109 of project.tsx)
The regex pattern uses bare '|sharp|' without word-boundary guards or context awareness, causing false positives on legitimate English prose in comments
Agent's legitimate work (mean pixel diff 2.43, 135 episodes, ~69 min of iteration) was entirely discarded due to this false positive anti-cheat trigger

Recommendation: Add \b word boundaries around 'sharp' in the regex, or better yet check for import/require statements rather than bare word matches, or strip comments before running the anti-cheat regex
